ratings_why.fun: Free early losses (0 hero damage in rounds 1-3) fill the pile while the Apprentice grows, and the late game has three clear routes to build toward, so the growth has a shape I'd enjoy climbing with.
ratings_why.distinct: A shared death pile shared out by a Fruit keyword plays unlike the Oozes' Eat or a Deathrattle tribe, though dying for value is a familiar auto-battler idea.

verdict_why: The core works; Moss-Bier's wording needs a fix, and White-Rot Renderer breaks the printed-only guard the runaway case relies on.

points.text: Moss-Bier Bearer's "it permanently gains +1/+1" can be read as the dying unit; say "this permanently gains +1/+1".

White-Rot Renderer feeds buffed stats into the Compost, so burying a Fruit carry beside Ludwig and a Bootlace run gives back more than it costs. Fine as a high roll, but the rationale's claim that 'growth never feeds its own source' no longer holds, so the owner should know.
Golden Warden Amanita only doubles Bristle, not her job; let her golden also destroy the units in front of and behind her, so it's worth chasing.
Rootbinder is dead text on a pure Guild board at Tier 4, the tier that should 'set up future things'; it could also give Fruit to Created Spores beside it, so it works with the Burst too.
Growth is bounded by printed stats, so it rises with tier rather than compounding: a healthy curve. Only golden Mourner turns it quadratic, which makes it the chase card of the tribe.

standouts.why: Candlesnuff Apprentice is a real seed: a Tier 1 that you keep all game because it drinks the pile every turn.
Grandmother Bootlace is a capstone the comp is built for, with a placement cost that burials keep fighting.
Mourner of Three Rains changes the pile's timing, which turns burials into an investment over several turns.

weakest.why: Rootbinder does nothing on a Guild-only board.
Stumpwick Puffling's 2/1 body (3 stats) is below the Tier 1 body of 4 and loses the early tempo fights it's meant to win.
Hired Mute is plain economy that Spores trigger almost every turn, with nothing to decide.

flags.note: Golden Mourner of Three Rains never empties the pile, so every Fruit gains a quarter of a pile that grows every turn: quadratic growth.
White-Rot Renderer composts buffed stats; with Ludwig and many Fruit units one burial returns more than it removes.
Candlesnuff Apprentice gains about 2 bodies a turn by mid-game, far over the Tier 1 target; the designer says it's on purpose.
Golden Old Fingers copies keep all stats, so six full copies of a pumped carry come back each fight.
It is unclear whether Moss-Bier Bearer or the dying unit gains the +1/+1.
